turns.content: Treat lambda = h/p as though it were the Stefan-Boltzmann relation for this electron. Explain the resulting inverse dependence on momentum without yet deriving the voltage dependence or evaluating a wavelength.
Convert eV to joules for this potential and compare the resulting kinetic energy with the electron rest energy.
Explain whether the nonrelativistic momentum is an adequate textbook approximation and what correction is being neglected.
Using the chosen approximation, calculate p=sqrt(2m_e eV).
Substitute the momentum into lambda=h/p and calculate the wavelength in metres.
Convert the result to picometres and state the nonrelativistic voltage scaling of the wavelength.
Check the units, order of magnitude, and direction of the relativistic correction.
Report the electron's magnetic susceptibility at 40 kV and predict it at 160 kV.
